{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script
#
# This is a self-submitting Flux script: run it directly (e.g., `./auto_encoder_type1.flux.sh`).
# It will submit itself to Flux with the translated resource requests.

# Translated resources from Slurm:
#   --nodes=1            -> -N 1
#   --ntasks-per-node=4  -> -n 4
#   --time=24:00:00      -> -t 24h
#   --gres=gpu:...:1     -> -g 1  (GPU model constraint not translated)
JOBID=$(flux batch -N 1 -n 4 -g 1 -t 24h --wrap "bash $0 __flux_inner")

echo "Submitted Flux job: $JOBID"

if [ "${1:-}" = "__flux_inner" ]; then
  # NOTE: Slurm --job-name=auto_encoder_type1 not translated.
  # Performance/ops implication: job identification may be less convenient; runtime performance is unaffected.

  # NOTE: Slurm --partition=Hercules not translated.
  # Performance implication: without a queue/constraint mapping, the job may run on any eligible resources; you are not forcing the Hercules partition.

  # NOTE: Slurm --mem-per-cpu=16G not translated.
  # Performance implication: without a per-core memory reservation/limit, the job may contend for memory or be OOM-killed, affecting reliability/performance.

  # NOTE: Slurm requested GPU model TitanV via --gres=gpu:TitanV:1.
  # Flux portable request only expresses GPU count (-g 1); no model constraint is applied.
  # Performance implication: job may run on a different GPU type, changing performance.

  module load pytorch/1.6.0-anaconda3-cuda10.2

  flux run -n 1 -g 1 pip install --no-index --upgrade pip
  flux run -n 1 -g 1 conda install -c akode atari-py

  # Run the main program within the allocation.
  flux run -n 4 -g 1 python Type_1.py
fi
"
